page.h1: HTS Chapter 74: Copper and Articles Thereof — Export Markets & Foreign Tariffs on U.S. Goods

seo.title: Tariff on U.S. Copper by Country: China, Canada, EU (HTS Ch. 74) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: What Mexico, Canada, the EU, Japan, China, Korea, Thailand and India charge on U.S. copper scrap, cathode, wire and tube, plus scrap-import rules.

intro: Tariffs on U.S. copper split three ways. **Scrap and cathode**, about two-thirds of the chapter, enter duty-free almost everywhere: in Mexico and Canada under USMCA, and in the EU, Japan, Korea, Thailand and, since February 2, 2025, India on copper and brass scrap. In these markets the buyer's scrap-import rules decide access (see each market's regulator). **China** is the exception: U.S. scrap and cathode pay 35% unless the importer holds an exclusion (0% + a 25% counter-tariff from 2018–2019 + a 10% extra duty), and wire, sheet and tube pay 29–40%. **Semi-finished copper** (wire, sheet, tube and fittings) pays 3% in Japan and Thailand and 5–10% in India. It is free in Korea under KORUS, free in the EU since July 1, 2026, and free in Canada, except refined copper wire, which has carried a 50% surtax since September 8, 2026.
valueBasis: FOB value of U.S. exports, as reported by the United States to UN Comtrade.

markets.rule: USMCA preferential tariff: 0% for U.S.-origin goods that meet the rules of origin. Chapter 74 was not part of Mexico's January 1, 2026 tariff increases

profile.headline: Mexico is the largest market ($3.96B, up 1.7%), mostly refined cathode (7403, $1.60B) and wire rod and wire (7408, $1.11B) for its wire, cable and auto-harness plants. Qualifying U.S. copper enters free under USMCA. Mexico's normal rates (5% on wire and stranded wire, up to 15% on sanitary ware) apply only if the rule of origin is not met, and its January 2026 tariff increases skipped copper.
profile.mainProducts: Refined copper & alloys, unwrought (cathode) (7403) · Copper wire (7408)

profile.headline: Canada ($2.44B, up 10.6%) buys scrap (7404, $850M) and anodes for its refineries (7402, $425M), plus wire (7408, $239M) and cathode (7403, $237M). Everything enters free under CUSMA except U.S. refined copper wire, which has paid a 50% surtax since September 8, 2026, even when it qualifies. A Canadian manufacturer that uses the wire in production can claim the surtax back.

profile.headline: The EU ($1.47B, up 66.2%) is almost all scrap (7404, $1.21B), shipped mainly to Belgium, Germany and Greece. Scrap and cathode were already duty-free. Since July 1, 2026 the EU also charges 0% on U.S. copper wire, sheet, tube and other semis, which normally pay 3–5.2%. The EU review clause that could restore duties after December 31, 2026 names only the steel and aluminum chapters, not copper.
profile.mainProducts: Copper waste & scrap (7404) · Copper plates, sheets & strip (7409)

regulator.name: EU Waste Shipment Regulation (Regulation (EU) 2024/1157)
regulator.requirement: Copper scrap for recycling is green-listed waste. From the U.S., an OECD country, it travels with the Annex VII information document and a contract with the EU recycler, with no prior consent needed. Refined copper and semis need no approval, and copper is not covered by the EU carbon border levy (CBAM)

profile.headline: China ($781M, down 73.4% from $2.94B) still buys mostly scrap (7404, $648M). U.S. scrap and cathode pay 35% unless the Chinese importer holds an exclusion, which runs only to December 31, 2026: China's 0% 2026 rate, plus the 25% counter-tariff from 2018–2019, plus the 10% extra duty. Scrap must also meet China's recycled-copper standards to enter at all.

regulator.name: Ministry of Ecology and Environment and General Administration of Customs (recycled copper raw-material rules)
regulator.requirement: Since November 15, 2024, copper and brass scrap enters only as recycled copper or copper-alloy raw material meeting national standards GB/T 38471 and GB/T 38470 (Announcement No. 23 of 2024). Grades may not be mixed in one declaration. Customs checks the cargo and its radiation level, and material it judges to be solid waste falls under China's solid-waste import ban

Since February 2, 2025 India has charged nothing on copper and brass scrap (2.5% before); cathode, bars, wire and sheet pay 5% and tube 7.5%. countryGuide.label: Country Commercial Guide: India import requirements

assumptions: Rates are what U.S.-origin goods pay in November 2026. They come from the WITS (TRAINS) simple-average MFN applied rate for one representative six-digit subheading per heading, the one with the largest 2025 U.S. exports in that heading (for example 7404.00 for scrap, 7403.11 for cathode, 7408.11 for wire rod and 7411.10 for refined tube), for 2023, the latest year WITS holds. They are updated where a national 2026 schedule or notice was checked: EU TARIC, China's 2026 provisional rates, India's February 2025 scrap notification and Canada's surtax orders. National 8–10-digit lines can differ.

Mexico, Canada and Korea show the free-trade-agreement rate for goods that qualify; the normal-rate column shows the MFN rate a non-qualifying good pays. Mexico's decree of December 29, 2025 raised no Chapter 74 line.
Canada's 7408 cells add the 50% surtax of the United States Surtax Order (2026) on refined copper wire (7408.11, 7408.19). Remission for wire used in Canadian manufacturing is on Export rules.
The EU cells show 0% for U.S.-origin goods under Regulation (EU) 2026/1455 from July 1, 2026; the normal-rate column shows the third-country duty other origins pay.

China's cells add three layers: China's 2026 rate (provisional where one exists, otherwise MFN), the 10% extra duty on all U.S. goods, and the 2018–2019 counter-tariff of the line (25%, 20% or 10%; another 5% on other unwrought refined copper and alloys from the September 2019 list). An importer with an exclusion pays only the first two.
India's cells show basic customs duty only. Its copper and brass scrap lines (7404 00 12, 7404 00 19, 7404 00 22) have been nil since February 2, 2025.
Trade agreements that are signed or announced but not in force (Thailand, Taiwan, Malaysia, India) are not applied; see Tariff updates.
